fact: The section 'It Can Be Lost' opens with 1 Kings 5:12, 'And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him...'
A time came when Solomon's wisdom was turned to foolishness
Proverbs 3:18 says 'She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her', the word retaineth being the point
Ecclesiastes 1:18 shows Solomon lost it: 'For in much wisdom is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow'
Solomon's joy was gone; he had tried everything to make himself happy, but happiness was not forthcoming
Solomon's beauty and dignity were reduced to vanity, and he lamented in Ecclesiastes 1:2 'Vanity of vanities, all is vanity', which the author glosses as asking what the benefit of life is
At that point in time Solomon had completely lost his mentality
When Solomon changed his God, God turned His back on him, and his journey to changing his God began with his losing his wisdom
1 Kings 3:3 says 'And Solomon loved the Lord...', which is the foundation of Solomon's relationship with God
1 Kings 4:29 shows the benefit of that relationship: God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore
1 Kings 5:4 shows the effect: 'But now the LORD my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent'
Solomon got very involved with God and the things of His kingdom, and built the tabernacle, which he dedicated amidst such glory from heaven
1 Kings 11:1 records that king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians and Hittites
God had said of those nations that they would surely turn away your heart after their gods, yet Solomon clave unto these in love
Solomon had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart
It was when Solomon was old that his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father
The LORD had appeared unto Solomon twice, and had commanded him that he should not go after other gods, but he kept not that which the LORD commanded
When Solomon began to love many strange women instead of God, God got angry with him and withdrew His wisdom from him
In the place of peace God stirred up an adversary against Solomon, and he lost control
The first adversary was Hadad the Edomite, who was of the king's seed in Edom, per 1 Kings 11:14
The second adversary was Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah, per 1 Kings 11:23
Rezon was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad did, and he abhorred Israel and reigned over Syria
Solomon the wisest suddenly became the most foolish till the end of his life, because he changed his God and God turned His back on him
One of the devil's greatest tools of defilement is pride
The moment things begin to work the tendency is to kiss your palm in the secret and say 'No one else except me. If I were not there, would it have worked?'
In the days of David the king, consulting Ahitophel was like consulting the Almighty Himself, but the day his counsel was rejected he went and hung himself
Suicide is called the height of madness, so at that point Ahitophel was the most foolish human being on planet earth, having lost his wisdom to self and pride

The author prays that wherever you would get to in life that would make you change your God, God will never allow you to get there, that the wealth that would make you change your God your hand may never touch, and that position you may never get

The author has told God: don't try me with what will hurt me, don't bless me with what will become a curse in my hands, leave me where you think is safest for me, and whatever will make my head get bigger than it is, don't let it reach my hand
The section 'Keep The Treasure!' quotes 2 Timothy 1:6-7,14, including 'For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind'
2 Timothy 1:14 says 'That good thing which was committed unto thee keep by the Holy Ghost which dwelleth in us'
A great treasure of wisdom has been deposited into your system, so it is your responsibility to keep it by the Holy Ghost
The devil is envious of that great treasure of divine wisdom on your inside
The gift of a sound mind will not work with the crooked, perverse, proud, nor with the defiled; it will only be sustained by those who live in the fear of the Lord
Jesus was a successful carrier of divine wisdom throughout His time, and the scriptures described Him as the wisdom and power of God, cited as 1 Corinthians 1:24
Jesus had the Spirit without measure, cited as John 3:34, and Romans 1:4 says He was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness
No crooked or perverse Christian has a future, and it takes integrity to earn dignity
The fear of the Lord is what constantly puts you on your toes, and it is your greatest security in your Christian adventure
The things that Solomon lost by changing his God, all the money he had could not restore back to him: he could not get his joy, peace and pleasantness back
Solomon started his journey as the wisest but ended as the most foolish, whereas Joseph made it, and Daniel, Apostle Paul and Jesus made it
The wisdom treasure from above glorifies its carrier, causing him or her to come out of obscurity into the limelight, so that you emerge a natural star on the earth
When God begins to show you the steps to take you cannot be compared with any natural man, no matter the effort he puts in
One striking insight is worth much more in value than a lifetime of struggles
